disease_label_per_paper: Acute chest syndrome evolving into acute respiratory distress syndrome in previously undocumented HbSC disease
presentation_summary: Presented with two days of bilateral flank pain, intermittent pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, nonproductive cough, and tactile fever.
Initial evaluation showed fever, tachycardia, tachypnea, hypoxemia with SpO2 88% on room air, anemia, reticulocytosis, and hyperbilirubinemia.
Initial chest radiograph and CT showed no active pulmonary disease.
He later developed high fever, worsening hypoxemia with SpO2 in the 70s on 4 L nasal cannula, labored breathing, and required intubation.
Repeat imaging showed extensive bilateral basilar airspace opacities and large evolving bilateral pleural effusions; PaO2/FiO2 was 88 mmHg.

risk_context.source_text_value: Hemoglobin electrophoresis later showed HbS and HbC; no documented hemoglobinopathy was known at presentation.
HbSC disease was confirmed after respiratory deterioration.

observations.source_text_value: Bilateral flank pain was present for two days.
Oxygen saturation dropped to the 70s on 4 L nasal cannula.
Heart rate was 120 beats per minute during deterioration.
Repeat imaging showed extensive bilateral basilar airspace opacities.
Large evolving bilateral pleural effusions were present.
Normocytic, normochromic anemia with hemoglobin 10 g/dL.
The paper states ACS evolved into ARDS; this event-hazard value represents presentation severity rather than outcome response.

course_observations.source_text_value: Initial SpO2 was 88% on room air; later deterioration is the rankable snapshot.
Initial chest radiograph and contrast-enhanced CT showed no active disease.
